query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by the formation of adiabatic shear bands (ASBs) and the resulting microstructural changes, such as grain refinement and increased dislocation density.
generation.conditions: In situ mechanical testing with atomic-resolution characterization
generation.mechanism: Formation of ASBs and resulting microstructural changes
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced mechanical properties, such as strength and ductility, due to the formation of ASBs and microstructural changes
generation.baseline: Quasi-static mechanical properties of solidified FeNiCrMn
generation.boundary: Temperature range: RT-1223 K, strain-rate range: 10^-5/s to 10^3/s
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between ASB formation and mechanical properties is not well understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: In situ mechanical testing with atomic-resolution characterization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no ASBs are formed during testing, and no significant microstructural changes are observed, then the hypothesis is falsified.

However, the mechanism of the special phenomenon for the high-entropy alloy deformed at high strain rates (beyond 1 × 103 s−1) is not clear yet. Serration characteristics are ubiquitous in many structural and functional materials such as high-entropy alloy (AlCoCr1.5Fe1.5NiTi0.5, Al0.3CoCrFeNi etc.). It would lead to the instability of mechanical properties. By studying the serration behavior, it may be possible to have an early warning signal for oncoming epileptic seizures and perhaps economic trends. In the present work, we used the split-Hopkinson pressure bar to investigate the dynamic mechanical behavior of NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy prepared by arc melting. The aims are: (1) To report the mechanical properties and microstructure under dynamic loadings, (2) to obtain the plastic model, and (3) to discuss the microstructural mechanism for the serration behavior when the alloy deforms at high strain rates.

decision.trend: Research on high- and medium-entropy alloys has focused on understanding their mechanical properties, including dynamic behavior, and the effects of composition, temperature, and strain rate on these properties. Studies have investigated the role of grain boundaries, precipitation, and lattice distortion on the deformation mechanisms and mechanical properties of these alloys. Recent work has also explored the use of advanced characterization techniques, such as in situ mechanical tests and atomic-resolution characterization, to understand the fundamental nature of physical mechanical phenomena like elastic instability and incipient plasticity.
decision.unsolved: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is not well understood, and the governing factors for its mechanical properties are not clearly identified. The effects of loading regime and material condition on the dynamic properties of FeNiCrMn are not fully understood, and the relationship between its microstructure and mechanical properties is not well established.
decision.lever: in situ mechanical testing with atomic-resolution characterization
decision.why: To investigate the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn, a controlled variable experiment using in situ mechanical testing with atomic-resolution characterization is proposed. This approach will allow for the examination of the alloy's microstructure and mechanical properties under various loading conditions, providing insights into the governing factors for its dynamic behavior. The use of advanced characterization techniques will enable the identification of the relationships between the alloy's microstructure, composition, and mechanical properties, ultimately leading to a better understanding of its dynamic behavior across temperature and strain-rate regimes.
